reviews.title: Disappointed: Great app ruined by extreme greed and aggressive paywalls
reviews.text:
I have been using CapCut for a long time for voice acting and various other projects. For a while, it was my go-to editor because it was fast, intuitive, and reliable. Unfortunately, I am beyond disappointed with what the app has become.
The current paywall situation is completely out of control. Basic tools and simple features that used to be free and essential to my workflow are suddenly locked behind a Pro subscription. It feels like every time the app updates, another standard feature gets paywalled. The pricing has gotten so greedy and aggressive that it genuinely feels like a cash-grab scheme rather than a legitimate editing tool.
It is frustrating to invest time into learning an app and building a workflow around it, only to be priced out of basic functionality. I used to recommend CapCut to everyone, especially fellow voice actors and creators, because of how dependable it was. Now, the app is barely usable without paying an outrageous subscription fee.
CapCut needs to seriously rethink its business model and fix its app before it drives away the entire community that made it popular in the first place. Until they stop locking basic features behind a paywall, I cannot recommend it.

It’s also frustrating that certain features, like Noise Reduction, are included on the phone app (where I started with CapCut a month or so ago), but on desktop, I need to upgrade to Pro to use it.

I should have just gone with Final Cut Pro or something. Wish I could get my money back.

reviews.title: From My Favorite App to My Biggest Disappointment
reviews.text:
I used to love CapCut and happily recommended it to other creators. Unfortunately, it has turned into what feels like a scam.

I originally purchased an annual subscription that was supposed to expire in April. Then I purchased another subscription, but instead of renewing in April, I was charged again in February and paid the full annual price all over again.

What makes this even worse is that I shoot all of my content in 4K. I can import my 4K videos into CapCut, edit them, but I can’t export them back in 4K with the subscription I already paid for. Instead, the app downgrades the quality of my own videos to 1080p unless I pay even more.

So after paying for a yearly subscription, I’m now expected to pay another $100 just to export my own 4K footage in the same quality I uploaded it. I genuinely don’t understand why I should have to spend over $200 a year just to trim videos, remove music, and make basic edits.

As a content creator, I need 4K exports for my work. I paid for this app, yet I still can’t use it for what I need. My refund request has not been resolved, and at this point it feels like I’ve simply thrown my money away.

Sadly, I won’t be using CapCut anymore. It’s incredibly disappointing to see an app I once loved become so aggressively monetized that even preserving the original quality of your own videos requires paying for another, even more expensive subscription.
